sec: Alport syndrome: collagen & type IV collagen table · p783

items.q: Alport syndrome is also known as hereditary nephritis and is caused by a mutation in:
opts: Collagen IV (COL4A5), most commonly a deletion
Collagen III (COL3A1), most commonly a point mutation
Nephrin (NPHS1), most commonly a missense mutation
items.exp: Alport syndrome = hereditary nephritis; the mutation is in collagen IV (COL4A5), with deletion as the commonest type. (Book p783)

items.q: Fill up: In Alport syndrome the commonest type of COL4A5 mutation is a ______.
items.exp: Mutation in collagen IV (COL4A5): the commonest is a deletion. (Book p783)

items.q: Match each type IV collagen heterotrimer with the basement membrane in which it is seen — 1) α1–α1–α2  2) α3–α4–α5  3) α5–α5–α6 … A) Seen from birth  B) Skin basement membrane  C) GBM, cochlea and ocular BM
items.exp: Type IV collagen table: α1-α1-α2 is seen from birth; α3-α4-α5 is found in the GBM, cochlea and ocular BM; α5-α5-α6 is found in skin basement membrane. (Book p783)

items.q: Alport syndrome damages the glomerular basement membrane, cochlea and ocular basement membrane but the skin basement membrane is spared in the classical form. Which collagen chain combination explains this distribution?
items.exp: The α3-α4-α5 heterotrimer is seen in the GBM, cochlea and ocular BM — the three sites involved in Alport syndrome. α5-α5-α6 marks skin basement membrane. (Book p783)

items.q: The α1–α1–α2 collagen IV trimer is present in basement membranes from birth.
opts: True — the table lists it under 'seen in: birth'
False — it appears only after 30 years of age
False — it is confined to the skin basement membrane
True, but only in patients with Alport syndrome
items.exp: The type IV collagen table lists α1-α1-α2 against 'birth'. (Book p783)

items.q: Which site is NOT listed as a location of the α3–α4–α5 collagen IV network?
items.exp: α3-α4-α5 is seen in GBM, cochlea and ocular BM; skin basement membrane contains α5-α5-α6. (Book p783)
